data_quality_notes: The Global Human Footprint dataset (Mu et al. 2022, Scientific Data) is distributed as GeoTIFF raster files on figshare and is not available as country-level aggregates through standard APIs (World Bank, WHO GHO). As a partial substitute, World Bank Agricultural Land (% of land area, indicator AG.LND.AGRI.ZS) was used as a proxy for the cropland component of the HFP composite index. This covers only one of eight HFP input layers (croplands); the full HFP also integrates built environments, population density, nighttime lights, pastures, roads, railways, and navigable waterways. The near-perfect theoretical alignment claimed by Mu et al. 2022 refers to the full composite HFP dataset. PHL is cross-sectional (2022 only); agricultural land matched to 2022. The negative direction is consistent with the hypothesis: more agricultural land implies more cropland within/near protected areas, reducing the PHL metric (% of protected area NOT covered by cropland/buildings).
summary: Using World Bank Agricultural Land (% of land area) as a partial proxy for the Global Human Footprint Index (cropland component only), bivariate Pearson r=-0.306 (p=0.0000), Spearman rho=-0.443 (p=0.0000), n=174 countries. Best functional form: quadratic. The negative direction is confirmed. The Mu et al. 2022 citation is credible (peer-reviewed Scientific Data); the full HFP composite would likely show a stronger relationship than this partial cropland-only proxy.
